image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a dark-shelled turtle, likely a mud turtle, partially buried in dry, cracked earth and leaf litter. The carapace is prominent, appearing smooth, dark brown/black, and slightly glossy with some algae or dirt patches. The head is tucked in but visible on the lower left, showing dark skin. One forelimb is visible extending from under the shell. The background consists of textured soil and dried leaves.

However, strictly speaking, the feature 'has three keels' is not visibly present as distinct structures.
